## Problem and numerical basis

The optimization minimizes the lean-solvent flow scale $s=L/L_{3\mathrm{C}}$ at a carbon dioxide capture target of 90%.
The scale multiplies the three liquid feeds together, preserving the nominal lean loading and unloaded amine mass fraction.
The calculation uses the 6 m case 3C bed, the twelve-state conserved model, 17 cosine nodes with upwind cells, and the equilibrium-manifold film with nine quadrature points.
The calculation retains the pre-joint-fit thermodynamic parameters used in the Stage 2 reference.
The nominal liquid inlet temperature of 318.15 K was imputed, and the caloric reference remains provisional.

The [baseline](results/runs/stage0_3c_n17_base_1972203/attempt.json) captured 89.4148804% at $s=1$.
The [constrained optimum](results/runs/stage2_3c_n17_problem_p/optimum.json) was $s^*=1.024745661793$, or 2.139726 kg/s of loaded lean liquid.
The Stage 3 comparisons test numerical reproducibility on this grid and the sensitivity of this optimum to changes in the input quantities.

## Second start

IPOPT started at $s=1.15$ with the same initial nodal profile as the constrained optimum.
The [second start](results/runs/stage3_3c_n17_second_start/attempt.json) converged to $s_2^*=1.024745587820$ in 31 iterations and 597.20 s.
The scaled residual infinity norm was $6.10\times10^{-12}$, and the physical certificate accepted the profile.
The difference $|s_2^*-s^*|=7.3973\times10^{-8}$ defines $\mathrm{tol}_s$ for the sensitivity comparisons.
It measures agreement between two starts on a fixed grid.
A sample late in the second start recorded 575 s of CPU time over 583 s of elapsed time, about 98.6% of one core.
The second start required 31 iterations, compared with five for the reference solve.

## Capture around the optimum (O4)

The ordinary column solver used separate case files with each liquid feed multiplied by the indicated solvent scale.
The initial bulk state used those same liquid CO₂ and water flows.
The cases use direct SI inputs, so the transport declaration does not restrict the case paths.

| Case | Solvent scale | Capture (%) | Wall time (s) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| [1% below optimum](results/runs/stage3_3c_n17_o4_low/attempt.json) | 1.014498205 | 89.7607166 | 117.86 |
| [Optimum](results/runs/stage3_3c_n17_o4_center/attempt.json) | 1.024745662 | 90.0000019 | 130.79 |
| [1% above optimum](results/runs/stage3_3c_n17_o4_high/attempt.json) | 1.034993118 | 90.2352449 | 125.62 |

All three solves passed numerical and physical certification.
The outer cases bracketed 90% capture, and $\eta(s^*)-0.90=+1.8625\times10^{-8}$ as a fraction, within the $10^{-7}$ feasibility tolerance.
The centered difference gave $d\eta/ds=0.23153470$, compared with $1/(\lambda_c F_{V,\mathrm{CO_2,in}})=0.23150360$.
The relative slope difference was 0.0134%, and the plan specifies no separate tolerance for slope agreement.

## Sensitivity checks (O5)

Each perturbed problem used the Stage 2 nodal profile and solvent scale as its starting point.
The capture target moved by $\Delta=0.005$ in capture fraction, the lean loading by $\Delta=0.005$ mol CO₂ per mol MEA, and the liquid inlet temperature by $\Delta=1$ K.
The lean-loading perturbation changes the CO₂ feed and holds the MEA and water feeds fixed.
Each direction used four re-solves at $-2\Delta$, $-\Delta$, $+\Delta$, and $+2\Delta$.

The exact scale derivative is $-\mathrm{lam}_p$ in each input coordinate.
For lean loading, the CO₂ coordinate derivative is multiplied by the nominal MEA molar feed.
The finite-difference check accepts a direction when
$$
\left|D_{\mathrm{exact}}-D_{\mathrm{FD}}(\Delta)\right|
\leq
\max\left(
\left|D_{\mathrm{FD}}(2\Delta)-D_{\mathrm{FD}}(\Delta)\right|,
2\,\mathrm{tol}_s/\Delta
\right).
$$

| Input direction | Multiplier | FD(Δ) | FD(2Δ) | Absolute error | Allowed error | Result |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Capture target (per fraction) | 4.31958725 | 4.3197567 | 4.32016869 | 0.000169451004 | 0.000411990504 | Pass |
| Lean loading (per mol CO₂/mol MEA) | 11.5666215 | 11.5197568 | 11.3819525 | 0.0468646946 | 0.137804269 | Pass |
| Liquid inlet temperature (per K) | 0.0102853337 | 0.0102897835 | 0.0103030003 | 4.44985732e-06 | 1.32168141e-05 | Pass |

All twelve perturbed solves passed numerical and physical certification.
The capture inequality remained active to the scaled feasibility tolerance, and the state and solvent-scale bounds remained inactive.
These comparisons support the multiplier derivatives for the tested directions on this mesh.

| Input direction | −2Δ wall time (s) | −Δ (s) | +Δ (s) | +2Δ (s) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Capture target | 144.43 | 148.76 | 124.84 | 120.78 |
| Lean loading | 158.74 | 146.18 | 127.57 | 133.79 |
| Liquid inlet temperature | 150.16 | 146.84 | 136.45 | 151.69 |

## Scope and retained evidence

The comparisons verify feasibility and first-order sensitivity for the local numerical optimum on the 17-node grid.
The mesh dependence of the optimum and sensitivities remains to be quantified.
The attempt files preserve the solver settings, the inlet basis, and physical certification.
The [summary](results/runs/stage3_3c_n17_summary.json) retains the calculated comparisons, individual perturbed optima, and wall times.
The first [low-flow attempt](results/runs/stage3_3c_n17_o4_low_interrupted/run.log) ended during a workspace routing interruption and the output recorder reported a JSON error for byte-valued worker output.
The successful retry supplied the low-flow value in the O4 table.
